picks.title: Why every agent needs a face
picks.excerpt: Builder.io argues designers should 'treat AI as your next user, not another feature' -- giving every agent a visible surface, state and personality instead of burying it behind a chat box.
picks.rationale: Turns vague 'design for agents' talk into a concrete UI stance — give the agent a surface, state and presence — that a product designer can apply to a screen tomorrow.

picks.title: The design handoff changed: here's what AI-legible specs look like
picks.excerpt: A practical breakdown of how the design handoff changes once a coding agent is the first reader: what 'AI-legible' specs, token naming and component contracts actually look like in a repo.
picks.rationale: Highest actionability in the pool: rewrites the artifact every design team ships daily — the spec — for a world where an agent, not a developer, reads it first.

picks.title: Motion for people who are scared of motion software
picks.excerpt: 'Motion for people who are scared of motion software' -- a Figma Motion walkthrough where the Figma agent generates a starting animation the designer then refines on canvas, with no After Effects round-trip.
picks.rationale: Shows the agent-generates-then-designer-refines loop working inside Figma Motion, removing the After Effects round-trip for UI animation — usable the same day.

picks.title: The trust test: four questions every tool (even Figma) should answer about AI training and model usage
picks.excerpt: A 'trust test' of four questions every design tool -- Figma included -- should be able to answer about how it trains on and uses customer work, framed for design leads doing vendor due diligence.
picks.rationale: Gives design leads a four-question checklist for AI-training due diligence — governance a team can run against its own tool stack this week.

picks.title: HP Z Captis 3D scanner gets an AI boost via Adobe Substance 3D Sampler
picks.excerpt: HP's Z Captis 3D scanner gains an AI boost through integration with Adobe Substance 3D Sampler, tightening the loop from physical object capture to production-ready materials and assets.
picks.rationale: A concrete capture-to-material pipeline shipping between two real products, pulling AI-assisted scanning into the industrial-design and 3D asset workflow.
